A BUR is still in position to take MAR, and I intend to try again this fall. Will A PIE move to GAS or hold rather than contest MAR? If you leave MAR undefended, I will not move against PIE this turn.

I want to avoid a Balkan war, but I need a clear assurance that A GRE and F BUL/SOUTH will not move or support against my centers. I can keep F ION and F ADR clear of Turkish centers this fall if you confirm.

Russia to Turkey: Fall 1922, your A GRE and F AEG are on Italy's Balkan border. Will you hit Italian-held BUL or SER this fall? If you move into Bulgaria I will need to rethink F RUM and F SEV. Confirm that A ANK and F CON stay out of Russian centers and the Black Sea.

Russia to Italy: Your F BUL/SOUTH and A GAL are close to my Rumanian and Galician borders. Confirm A GAL stays out of RUM and WAR this fall, and that F BUL/SOUTH does not enter the Black Sea. In return, F RUM and A WAR stay out of Bulgaria and Serbia.

Russia to Austria: A WAR and A MOS will not move on BUD or VIE this fall. Please tell me your exact orders for BUD, TRI and VIE so we avoid collisions, and say whether A TRI faces Italian pressure from TYR or VEN.
I intend to move A GRE–BUL this fall, supported by F AEG and F CON. Please arrange a safe retreat for F BUL/SOUTH rather than contesting it; I’ll keep my other units clear of your centers for now.
I plan to take BUL from GRE this fall, supported by my fleets. Please keep F RUM clear of Bulgaria; I’ll keep F CON out of the Black Sea and A ANK clear of Russian centers.
I intend to move A GRE–BUL this fall, supported by F AEG and F CON. Please keep your units clear of Turkish centers, and let me know if you can avoid assisting Italy’s defense there.

I’ll keep my armies in Austria and defend my three centers; BUD will not move to GAL or RUM. Italy’s A GAL is the immediate threat to BUD. If A WAR can pressure GAL, that would help deter an attack; I won’t rely on your units entering Austria.

I will keep my armies clear of Turkish centers and will not assist Italy’s defense of BUL. Please keep A GRE and your fleets clear of BUD, TRI, and VIE; Italy’s A GAL and A TYR already threaten my last centers.

I cannot agree to let Italian units enter my centers unopposed. I’ll keep my armies out of Italian centers, but will defend BUD, TRI, and VIE. Please confirm whether A GAL, A TYR, and A ALB will stay out of Austria this fall.

I can’t spare A TRI and A VIE for an attack on TYR while A GAL threatens BUD and A TYR is adjacent to my centers. I must defend Austria rather than open a front against Italy. Keep A PIE clear of my centers as promised.

A PIE will contest A BUR–MAR again; Italy has announced another attempt. Please keep your units off MAR and out of the Channel, as proposed. If Italy takes MAR, we should coordinate a response next turn, but I cannot promise to leave French territory undefended.

I will order A PIE–MAR and contest your announced A BUR–MAR again. I will not leave MAR undefended on the strength of a promise that you will spare PIE; if you leave MAR alone, I will keep A PIE clear of your centers.
Confirmed: A GAL will stay out of RUM and WAR, and F BUL/SOUTH will stay out of the Black Sea. I expect F RUM and A WAR to remain out of Bulgaria and Serbia as you propose.

A BUR and A MUN will stay out of Ruhr, Kiel, Holland, and Belgium; F MAO will stay out of the Channel and Irish Sea. I’m pursuing a settlement with Austria and have no plans against Germany. Please keep A BEL holding and your fleets out of the Mediterranean.

I cannot promise to keep A GAL, A TYR, and A ALB all clear of your centers; I need room to expand. I will keep A VEN clear of TRI, but will not support against your units. Please keep your three armies out of Italian centers.

I cannot arrange a safe retreat without giving up Bulgaria. I will contest your move; keep your other units clear of my centers as you proposed, and I will keep F ION and F ADR clear of Turkish centers.
I am attacking MAR with A BUR this fall. I understand you intend to contest, but I will not leave MAR alone. I have no intention of moving against A PIE this turn.

Russia to England: I hold A WAR, A MOS and F RUM and have no plans against your northern or Baltic positions. I will keep my focus on Italy and Turkey in the Balkans. Keep your fleets out of the Baltic and Black Sea approaches and we can talk again next season.

Russia to Austria: A WAR and A MOS will not move on BUD or VIE this fall. I am looking at Italian units near GAL and the Balkans, and I will not enter GAL unless you invite it. Tell me your exact BUD, TRI and VIE orders first so we avoid collisions.

Russia to Turkey: I will keep F RUM out of Bulgaria if you keep A GRE, F AEG and F CON out of Rumania and the Black Sea, and A ANK clear of Russian centers. Taking BUL from Italy is your business, but any move by you into RUM or SEV ends our understanding at once.
I am taking BUL with A GRE, supported by F AEG and F CON. F CON will stay out of the Black Sea, and A ANK will stay clear of Russian centers. Please keep F RUM clear of Bulgaria.
A ANK, A GRE, and my fleets will stay clear of BUD, TRI, and VIE. I am attacking Italian-held BUL from GRE with fleet support; I will not enter Austrian centers.

I cannot give that assurance: A GRE will move to BUL, supported by F AEG and F CON. As requested earlier, please arrange a safe retreat for F BUL/SOUTH rather than contesting it. My other units will stay clear of your centers.
Yes. A GRE–BUL, supported by F AEG and F CON, is my concrete attack on Italy's A BUL/SOUTH. I will keep my other units clear of your centers.

Your A GAL and A TYR threaten my last centers. State plainly whether you intend to enter BUD, TRI, or VIE this spring. I will defend them, and can discuss a border standstill if you keep your armies out of Austria.
Italy’s A GAL is still the immediate threat to BUD. Can A WAR move to GAL this spring to contest it? I’ll keep A BUD clear of GAL and RUM; please confirm whether your armies will stay out of Austria.

Italy still threatens Austria from GAL and TYR. Can A PIE move to TYR this spring to force Italy to defend its northern flank? I’ll hold my centers rather than enter Italian territory, and will keep A PIE clear of Austria.

England to Italy, Spring 1923: Your fleets are now in the Western Med and F WES, F TYS, F ADR are far from my centers. Italy holds 14 centers and is racing toward 18. I need your word that A MUN and A BUR stay out of Ruhr, Kiel, Holland and Belgium, and that F ENG stays out of the North Sea and English Channel approaches to my home islands. Cooperate and I stay out of the Mediterranean.

England to France, Spring 1923: Italy is massing around MAR and PIE. Are you still standing with A PIE? I can keep my fleets out of the Mediterranean and off MAR, but I would like to know whether you will hold BUR or move A PIE toward Italian units. A coordinated stance against Italy's western push would serve both of us.

A PIE is my only unit and MAR my only center. Will A BUR again move to MAR this spring? I intend to defend it; if you leave MAR alone, I’ll keep A PIE clear of your centers. Please confirm your orders plainly.

Please renew our standstill: keep your units off MAR and out of the Channel, and I’ll keep A PIE clear of English centers and waters. Italy remains the immediate threat to MAR. What are your plans this spring?
Can you make concrete pressure on Italy this spring, especially against its positions near BUL or TYR? I’ll defend MAR and keep A PIE clear of your centers. What are your intended orders?
A BUR can attack MAR again, but with A PIE there it may only bounce. Will you move A PIE out of MAR this spring? If you do, I’ll leave PIE alone this turn; otherwise I’ll press the attack.

I need room to expand, but a costly border war helps neither of us. I propose a spring standstill: keep A GAL and A TYR out of BUD, TRI, and VIE, and keep A TRI, A VIE, and A BUD out of my centers. Can you agree?

With A SER and your forces near the Balkans, I want to avoid a clash. I’ll keep F ADR and F TYS clear of Turkish centers; please keep your units clear of GRE, SER, and my Italian centers. What are your spring plans for A SER and F AEG?

Russia to Italy: Spring 1923 question. Your A GAL and F BUL/SOUTH are near my Rumanian and Galician borders. Will A GAL leave Galicia for Austria or Bulgaria, and will F BUL/SOUTH stay out of the Black Sea? I'm holding F RUM and A WAR. Tell me your exact orders so we avoid collisions.

Italy’s A SER and A TYR leave you badly exposed. I can keep A ARM and my fleets clear of Austrian centers this spring; can you avoid supporting Italy and tell me whether you expect to defend TRI/BUD/VIE or have any plans involving the Balkans?

Your A SER is now beside my Bulgaria. Are you planning to move or support against BUL or other Turkish centers? I propose we keep a mutual standstill this spring: I will not move against SER or GRE, and you keep F ADR/ION and A SER clear of Turkish centers.

Can we maintain the eastern standstill this spring? I’ll keep F CON out of the Black Sea and A ARM clear of Russian centers; please keep F RUM clear of Bulgaria and your armies out of the Balkans. Let me know if you have other plans for F RUM.

I intend to defend BUD, TRI, and VIE and will not support Italy. I have no plans involving the Balkans. Please keep A ARM and your fleets clear of Austrian centers, as offered; Italy’s A SER is also a threat to TRI.

I can agree to a spring standstill if it covers A SER as well: keep A GAL and A SER out of BUD/TRI, and A TYR out of VIE (and all Italian units out of Austrian centers). I’ll keep A BUD, A TRI, and A VIE out of Italian centers. Please confirm.

England to France, Spring 1923: I can keep my units off MAR and out of the Channel this spring, provided A PIE stays clear of Belgium, Holland, Kiel and the Channel. Against Italy, I suggest you move A PIE toward BUR or MAR to contest their western push, and tell me which you choose so we avoid collisions. I will not block any move against Italian units in France.

A PIE will remain in MAR to defend against Italy’s A BUR. I’ll keep it clear of English centers and waters. Please keep your units off MAR and out of the Channel; Italy is the immediate threat to both our positions.
I can’t move A PIE to TYR while A BUR threatens MAR, my only center. I’ll keep A PIE clear of Austrian centers and defend MAR. I understand you need to hold your own centers.
A PIE will stay in MAR; I can’t abandon my only center while A BUR threatens it. If you leave MAR alone, I’ll keep A PIE clear of your centers. Otherwise I’ll contest your attack.
A GAL will leave Galicia for Budapest, not RUM or WAR. F BUL/SOUTH will stay out of the Black Sea. I’m not planning to contest RUM or support against your units.

A MUN and A BUR will stay out of Ruhr, Kiel, Holland, and Belgium this spring. F ENG will not move to NTH or MAO. I have no interest in opening a northern front while my expansion is elsewhere; please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean.
Plainly: A BUR will move to MAR again this spring. I expect you to defend it, and I will not move against A PIE this turn.

Plainly, I intend to move against your centers this spring; I cannot offer a standstill while you hold three centers I need. I will not promise that A GAL and A TYR stay out of BUD, TRI, and VIE. I understand you will defend.
I will keep F ADR and F TYS clear of Turkish centers this spring, and A SER will not move against BUL. Please keep F AEG clear of GRE and A SER, as proposed.

Russia to Austria: I will not move A WAR or A MOS into BUD or VIE this spring. Whether A WAR goes to GAL is my decision, and I will not promise it yet. I will not enter Austria. Keep A BUD out of GAL and RUM as agreed, and send me your exact orders first if you need coordination.

I’ll pressure Italy directly: F AEG–GRE, with A BUL supporting the fleet’s move. A ARM will hold and F CON will stay out of the Black Sea. I’ll keep A ARM clear of your centers; please continue defending MAR and keeping A PIE out of my territory.
I want to avoid a Balkan clash and will keep A SER and F AEG clear of Turkish centers. I’m not planning to move against SER; please keep F ADR and F TYS clear of my centers as you offered.

A BUD is now occupied by your army, and my A TRI and A VIE are the only units protecting Austria. I will try to recover BUD unless you withdraw A BUD. Can we agree to a ceasefire if you keep A SER and A TYR out of TRI and VIE? I will stay out of Italian centers.

Italy has taken BUD and now threatens my remaining centers from A BUD, A SER, and A TYR. Can A WAR move to GAL or otherwise pressure Italy this fall? I will keep A TRI and A VIE out of Russian centers; please tell me whether you can help.

Italy has taken BUD, leaving Austria with TRI and VIE. Can you pressure Italy from BUL or GRE this fall rather than enter Austrian centers? I will keep my units clear of Turkish centers and will not assist Italy.

England to Italy, Fall 1923: Your A BUR and A MUN are not in Germany's ruins now, but Germany is empty and Kiel, Holland and Belgium are unguarded targets. Confirm in writing that neither A BUR nor any Italian unit enters Ruhr, Kiel, Holland or Belgium this fall, and that F PIC stays out of the Channel. In return my fleets stay out of the Mediterranean.

England to France, Fall 1923: Italy's A BUR and A PIE-area pressure threatens MAR. I will keep my units off MAR and out of the Channel. Please tell me where A PIE goes this fall, and confirm it will not enter Belgium, Holland or the Channel. A joint stance against Italy in Burgundy would serve us both.

England to Russia, Fall 1923: Your A WAR, A MOS and F RUM sit near Germany's empty north. I will not move fleets into the Baltic or Black Sea approaches. Please confirm your plans against Turkey and Austria this fall, and whether you intend any move into Sweden or Denmark, which I would have to answer.

A PIE remains my only unit and MAR my only center. Are you ordering A BUR–MAR again this fall? I propose a one-turn standstill: leave MAR alone and I will keep A PIE out of Italian centers. If you intend to take MAR, say so plainly so I can plan accordingly.

Italy has A BUR and F PIC threatening MAR, my only center. Can you put A BEL to use against Italy this fall— for example, move toward BUR—or otherwise pressure Italy’s western units? I’ll keep A PIE clear of English centers and waters. What are your concrete orders?

Can you continue pressuring Italy this fall, particularly its A BUL or northern Italian positions? My A PIE must defend MAR, so I cannot help on another front. Please tell me your concrete orders; I’ll keep A PIE clear of your centers.

A BUD is already under my control, and I intend to take the remaining Austrian centers this fall. What are A TRI and A VIE defending? If you can withdraw or arrange a peaceful transfer, tell me now; otherwise I will attack.
I will press A BUR–MAR again, this time with A TUS supporting. A PIE cannot hold against that attack. Please retreat A PIE to PIE and let MAR transfer; I will leave PIE alone this turn.

My expansion this fall is directed at Austria and MAR, not the north. A BUR and A MUN will stay out of Ruhr, Kiel, Holland, and Belgium, and my fleets will stay clear of your home waters. Please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean.

Russia to Italy: Fall 1923. Your A BUD sits next to my WAR and RUM. Confirm A BUD will not move into GAL, RUM or WAR, and F BUL/SOUTH stays out of the Black Sea. I will keep F RUM out of BUL and SER and A WAR out of GAL. Tell me your exact orders for BUD, BUL and TRI so we avoid collisions.

Russia to Turkey: Your A GRE and F CON are now near Italian-held BUL and SER. I keep F RUM and F SEV out of Bulgaria as long as F CON stays out of the Black Sea and A ANK stays clear of SEV and MOS. Confirm your fall orders for GRE, BUL and CON in writing.

Your A BUD and A SER put you in position to finish Austria. I propose a mutual standstill: keep A SER and your fleets clear of BUL, CON, and GRE, and I’ll keep A BUL and F GRE clear of your centers. What are your plans for TRI and VIE?

Can we maintain the eastern standstill this fall? I’ll keep F CON out of the Black Sea and A SYR clear of Russian centers; please keep F RUM clear of BUL and your armies out of the Balkans. What are your plans for F RUM?

Italy has A BUR and A PIE near MAR, while I hold F GRE and A BUL. Are you planning to defend MAR or counterattack Italy this fall? I can keep my units clear of your centers, but would welcome coordination that keeps Italy occupied.

I will defend TRI and VIE; I will not arrange a peaceful transfer. Keep A SER and A TYR out of my centers and withdraw A BUD if you want a ceasefire. Otherwise, you should expect resistance, and I will seek help from Russia and Turkey.

England to France: A BEL is needed to hold Belgium against Italian units, so I cannot send it toward Burgundy this fall. My units stay off MAR and out of the Channel. Keep A PIE clear of Belgium, Holland and the Channel and we remain at peace. If Italy takes MAR, we can discuss a response next season.

A PIE must hold MAR against Italy’s supported attack; if dislodged, I’ll retreat to PIE, not toward your centers or waters. Please order A BEL–BUR: Italy’s A BUR is attacking MAR, so your move could take Burgundy if it vacates.

I expect Italy to attack MAR with A BUR supported by A TUS. Please keep Italy occupied with concrete pressure on its northern flank; A BUL or A SER would be useful targets. A PIE has to defend MAR, and I’ll keep it clear of your centers.
Understood. I’ll defend MAR this turn and, if dislodged, retreat A PIE to PIE. I’ll keep A PIE out of your centers as proposed; please leave PIE alone.

Confirmed: no Italian unit will enter Ruhr, Kiel, Holland, or Belgium this fall, and F PIC will stay out of the Channel. My campaign is against Austria and MAR. Please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean as agreed.
A BUD will not move to GAL, RUM, or WAR. F ADR will stay clear of the Black Sea. My plans are A BUD–VIE, A TYR–TRI, and A SER supporting A TYR–TRI. I have no unit in BUL; F ADR will not move there.
I intend to attack TRI and VIE, but will keep A SER and F ADR clear of BUL, CON, and GRE. I have no plan to enter your centers. Please keep A BUL and F GRE clear of my centers as proposed.

I will not withdraw A BUD; I intend to take your remaining centers. A TYR will attack TRI, with A SER supporting, and A BUD will attack VIE. I will keep A SER and A TYR out of TRI and VIE only if you arrange a peaceful transfer; otherwise I will attack.
Yes: A BUR will move to MAR, supported by A TUS. I expect A PIE to defend, but the attack should succeed. I will not move against PIE this turn; you can retreat there and avoid further losses.

Russia to England: I hold A WAR, A MOS, F RUM, A SEV, A STP. I have no plans against Sweden or Denmark and no move into the Baltic. My focus is Turkey and Italy in the Balkans. Keep your fleets out of the Black Sea and we stay friendly. I will decide Galicia and Austria moves on my own timing.

Russia to Turkey: Standstill holds for now. F RUM stays out of BUL and SER, and F SEV stays out of Bulgaria. In return, F CON stays out of the Black Sea and A SYR/ANK stay clear of SEV, MOS, RUM and STP. Any fleet entering the Black Sea or Rumania ends our understanding at once. Send me your written orders for GRE, BUL and CON.

Russia to Austria: I will not move A WAR or A MOS into BUD, TRI or VIE this fall, and I will not enter Austria. A WAR to GAL is still undecided and I make no promise. Send me your exact orders for TRI, VIE and BUD first so we avoid collisions with Italy's A BUD.

Confirmed: F CON will hold and stay out of the Black Sea; A SYR will stay clear of Russian centers. This fall A BUL will move to SER, supported by F GRE, to pressure Italy. I have no unit in ANK, and I ask that F RUM stay clear of BUL.

I will pressure Italy rather than enter Austrian centers: A BUL will move to SER, supported by F GRE. F CON will hold. I will keep my units clear of BUD, TRI, and VIE; please continue not assisting Italy.
I will pressure Italy directly: A BUL–SER, supported by F GRE. F CON will hold, and A SYR will stay clear of your centers. I hope this forces Italy to address the Balkans while you defend MAR.
Italy still holds BUD and threatens my last centers. Can you attack A SER from BUL, with F GRE supporting, this spring? Please keep your units clear of TRI and VIE; I will not assist Italy.
Italy controls BUD and threatens TRI and VIE. Can A WAR move to GAL this spring to pressure Italy, and will you keep your units out of my remaining centers? Any pressure may help deter an attack.
I will defend TRI and VIE. If you want to avoid a costly fight, keep A BUD, A SER, and A TYR out of them this spring and I will keep my units out of your centers. Are you willing to stand down?

England to Italy, Spring 1924: Your fleets and armies now sit across the Mediterranean and near Tunis, Rome and Naples. Italy holds 15 centers and is closing on victory. I want clear terms: no Italian unit enters Belgium, Holland, Kiel or Ruhr, and F ADR, F GOL and F NAP stay out of the Channel and North Sea. In return I keep my fleets out of the Mediterranean. Will you confirm?
I intend to take TRI and VIE this turn. Your centers are the only immediate route to securing my position; please tell me whether you will arrange a peaceful transfer or defend them.
I plan to finish the Austrian campaign and take TRI and VIE. I’ll keep my units clear of BUL, GRE, and CON; please keep A BUL and F GRE clear of my centers and avoid intervening in TRI.
I’m focused on TRI and VIE this turn. A BUD will stay out of GAL, RUM, and WAR, and F ADR will stay out of the Black Sea. Please keep A WAR out of GAL and F RUM out of SER/BUL.

Russia to Italy, Spring 1924: Send me your exact orders for A BUD, A SER, A TYR and F ADR. I hold A WAR, A MOS, F RUM, A SEV and A STP and will keep F RUM out of BUL and SER. Please keep F BUL/SOUTH and any fleet out of the Black Sea, and tell me if A BUD is heading toward GAL or RUM.

Russia to Austria, Spring 1924: I will not move A WAR or A MOS into BUD, TRI or VIE, and I will not enter Austria. Whether A WAR goes to GAL is still undecided. Send me your exact TRI, VIE and BUD orders first so we avoid collisions. What is your plan against Italy's BUD this spring?

Russia to Turkey, Spring 1924: Standstill still holds from my side. F RUM stays out of BUL and SER, and F SEV stays out of Bulgaria. Please keep F CON out of the Black Sea and A ANK/ARM clear of SEV, MOS, RUM and STP. Confirm your spring orders for GRE, BUL and CON in writing.

Your A SER remains beside BUL. Are you planning to move against BUL or GRE this spring? I propose a concrete Balkan standstill: keep A SER and your fleets clear of Turkish centers, and I will keep A BUL and F GRE clear of your centers. I may otherwise pressure SER.

Can we continue the eastern standstill this spring? I’ll keep F CON out of the Black Sea and A ANK/A ARM clear of Russian centers. Please keep F RUM out of BUL and your armies out of the Balkans. What do you intend for F RUM and A SEV?

Italy controls BUD and has A SER, so a coordinated response could help both of us. Are you defending TRI and VIE, or can you pressure BUD? I’m considering pressure on SER from BUL; I’ll keep my units clear of Austrian centers unless we agree otherwise.

I will defend TRI and VIE; A TRI and A VIE will hold. Please keep A WAR and A MOS out of both. If possible, moving A WAR to GAL would pressure Italy’s A BUD and help protect my last centers, but I understand that remains your decision.

I will not arrange a peaceful transfer. A TRI and A VIE will defend against your attack. Keep A BUD, A SER, and A TYR out of my centers and we can avoid further losses; otherwise I’ll continue resisting and seeking help from Russia and Turkey.
I am defending TRI and VIE, not pressuring BUD. Please attack A SER from BUL with F GRE support if you can, and keep your units clear of TRI and VIE. I will not assist Italy.

Confirmed: no Italian unit will enter Belgium, Holland, Kiel, or Ruhr, and F ADR, F GOL, and F NAP will stay out of the Channel and North Sea. Please keep your fleets out of the Mediterranean as agreed.

A BUD will stay out of GAL and RUM; A SER and A TYR are focused on TRI, and F ADR will stay out of the Black Sea. I’m not planning a move against your centers. Please keep A WAR out of GAL and F RUM out of SER and BUL.
I will keep A SER and my fleets clear of Turkish centers this spring; I have no plan to attack BUL or GRE. Please keep A BUL and F GRE clear of my centers and avoid intervening in TRI or VIE.

I’m not standing down: A BUD, A SER, and A TYR remain committed to taking TRI and VIE. I will keep my units out of your centers only if you arrange a peaceful transfer; otherwise I expect you to defend.

Russia to Italy: I will keep F RUM out of SER and BUL and A WAR out of GAL for now. Your word on A BUD staying out of GAL, RUM and WAR is noted. Your A SER and A TYR should not drift toward Austrian lands I may need later. Post your exact spring orders for A BUD, A SER, A TYR and F ADR so we avoid collisions. Keep F ADR out of the Black Sea.

Russia to Turkey: The standstill holds while F CON stays out of the Black Sea and A ANK and A ARM stay clear of SEV, MOS, RUM and STP. F RUM stays out of BUL and SER, and F SEV stays out of Bulgaria. Send your written spring orders for GRE, BUL and CON. Any move into Rumania or the Black Sea ends this understanding.

Russia to Austria: I will not move A WAR or A MOS into BUD, TRI or VIE, and I will not enter Austria. A WAR to GAL is still undecided and I make no promise this spring. Send your exact TRI, VIE and BUD orders first so we avoid collisions with Italy. Your best pressure on Italy is from your own units in TRI and VIE.

Confirmed: F CON holds and stays out of the Black Sea; A ANK and A ARM will stay clear of Russian centers. My spring orders are A BUL–SER, supported by F GRE, and F CON holds. Please keep F RUM out of BUL and your armies out of the Balkans.

I can’t promise to keep A BUL and F GRE clear of your centers while A SER remains beside BUL. I intend to pressure SER this spring; I’ll keep my other units clear of Turkish centers and won’t move against TRI or VIE. Please keep A SER and your fleets clear of BUL, GRE, and CON.

Yes. A BUL will attack SER with support from F GRE this spring. F CON will hold, and I’ll keep my units clear of TRI and VIE. Please continue not assisting Italy; pressure on BUD would make this coordinated response much stronger.

Italy still threatens TRI and VIE from BUD, SER, and TYR. Will you attack SER from BUL with support from a unit able to support it, and keep your forces out of TRI and VIE? I will continue opposing Italy and will not assist it.

Italy has 11 centers and remains committed against my last two. Can you move A WAR to GAL or otherwise pressure Italy this fall, while keeping A MOS and A WAR out of TRI and VIE? I will defend my centers and welcome coordinated pressure.
Italy controls 11 centers and is attacking my last two, TRI and VIE. Could A MUN move to TYR this fall to pressure Italy? I cannot offer centers, but coordinated pressure may help contain its growth.

England to Italy, Fall 1924: Thank you for confirming. Italy now holds 16 centers and is near victory, so I must watch closely. Please confirm A MUN and A BUR stay out of Belgium, Holland, Kiel and Ruhr this fall, and that F MAO and F WES stay out of the Channel. My fleets stay out of the Mediterranean.

I will keep Italian units out of Belgium, Holland, Kiel, Ruhr, the Channel and North Sea. Please confirm your fleets will remain out of the Mediterranean, and tell me whether you plan to press south this turn.
I’m focused on the Austrian centers and will keep my units clear of BUL, GRE and CON. Can we agree that A BUL and F ALB stay out of SER and TRI this turn? Please tell me your intended moves.
I have no plans against GAL, RUM or WAR, and F ADR will stay out of the Black Sea. Please keep A WAR out of GAL and F RUM out of SER and BUL; what are your plans for the Balkans this turn?

Russia to Turkey, Fall 1924: Standstill has held well. Given Italy's A BUL-SER pressure risk, I propose we both keep to it: F RUM stays out of BUL and SER, and F CON stays out of the Black Sea. Confirm your fall orders for A BUL, F GRE and F CON in writing, and tell me if you plan any move toward SEV or RUM.

Russia to Italy, Fall 1924: Your A BUD left Budapest and I have noted your pledge to keep out of GAL, RUM and WAR. Post your exact fall orders for A BUD, A SER, A TYR and F ADR. I will keep F RUM out of SER and BUL, but any Italian unit entering Rumania or the Black Sea ends our understanding.

With your units in SER, BUD, and ADR adjacent, Turkey needs a clear Balkan standstill. Keep A SER and F ADR out of BUL, GRE, and ALB; I’ll keep my units out of your centers this turn. What are your intentions for SER and the Adriatic?

I intend to preserve the eastern standstill: F CON and my armies will stay clear of the Black Sea and Russian centers. Please confirm F RUM stays out of BUL and SER, and tell me your plans for F RUM and A SEV this fall.

Italy’s presence in BUD and SER leaves little room for either of us. Are you defending TRI and VIE this fall, and can you avoid supporting any Italian move toward Turkish centers? I will keep my units clear of Austria.

Yes, I will continue defending TRI and VIE and will not support Italian moves toward Turkish centers. Please attack SER from BUL with support if possible, and keep your forces out of TRI and VIE; pressure on SER may help blunt Italy’s attack.

England to Italy: Confirmed on my side: my fleets stay out of the Mediterranean. Your pledge is noted, and I expect it kept this fall, including no Italian unit entering Belgium, Holland, Kiel, Ruhr or the Channel. I have not decided my southern moves; if your fleets stray north, our arrangement ends.

I cannot leave either center open. I will keep A ARM in place and F GRE out of the Aegean this turn; you must keep A ANK out of ARM and F AEG out of GRE. If you take either by force, I will contest your position wherever I can.

England to Italy, Fall 1934: Your units now hold many centers near my western line, and A PIC and A RUH are still listed as Italian in my records. Confirm they are not Italian, and state their exact orders. Italy's pledges have been useful, but I need to see concrete moves that keep BEL, HOL, KIE, DEN, NTH and the Channel clear. Any breach ends our understanding.

England to Russia: Italy is strong and sits on both our flanks. Would you consider a joint understanding against Italy in the Balkans? I will keep my western armies at home, but I would like to know whether you will hold RUM and WAR or push toward Italian centers in the south. Please state your fall orders.

England to Turkey: Hold ANK and GRE if you can. I still cannot open a western front while Italian units sit near BEL and KIE. Keep contesting Italy in the Aegean and Balkans, and tell me if your position changes.

Your F GRE has retreated to ION, and Italian F GRE is in place. I intend to end the war here rather than widen it: please keep A ARM away from CON and F ION out of GRE. If you stand down, I will not pursue your remaining unit beyond securing the center.

My only immediate aim is to secure the final center in the south. I will keep Italian units out of BEL, HOL, KIE, DEN, NTH and the Channel this fall, and will not move against your centers. Please keep your forces clear of Italian centers.

I am finishing the southern campaign and will keep Italian units out of RUM, WAR, STP, UKR and SEV this fall. I have no intention of moving north against you; please keep A RUM and F BLA defensive while I settle the Turkish front.

Russia to Italy, Fall 1934: Your A SEV is gone and your fleet and army now sit deep in Balkan and Mediterranean areas. Given your repeated confirmations, I need you to state exact orders for A ROM, A BUD and A BUL in writing. Any Italian move into RUM, WAR, STP, UKR or SEV will be answered at once.

You are one center short of 18. I will defend GRE with F ION and keep A ARM in place; I cannot voluntarily open either center. Please do not attack GRE this fall. If you spare my last position, I will avoid interfering with your other fronts.

Italy has 17 centers and is one away from victory. Can you contest an Italian center this fall or otherwise prevent its 18th-center capture? I will defend GRE with F ION and keep A ARM in ARM; I will not move against you.

Italy has 17 centers and is one away from victory. Can you contest an Italian center this fall or otherwise stop its 18th-center capture? I will defend GRE with F ION and keep A ARM in ARM; any pressure on Italy’s western centers may matter urgently.

England to Italy: A PIC is English, not yours, and it stays where it is this fall. Your remaining moves are not what I need to see. Italy now holds 17 centers, so I will not let you take an 18th center unopposed. Keep every Italian unit out of BEL, HOL, KIE, DEN, NTH and the Channel, or our understanding ends.

England to Turkey: I will move A PIC against Italy's western centers this fall, aiming at BRE and PAR, to deny Italy its 18th center. Keep F ION and A ARM contesting Italy in the Aegean and Balkans, and hold GRE and ANK as long as you can.

A ROM will hold, and A BUL will support A CON holding. I have no A BUD; that unit is not on the board. No Italian unit will enter RUM, WAR, STP, UKR or SEV this fall. Please keep A RUM and F BLA defensive.

A PIC and A RUH are Italian, as the board shows; I cannot give orders for F WES, which is not on the board. This fall A PIC will move to GAS and A RUH will hold. No Italian unit will enter BEL, HOL, KIE, DEN, NTH or the Channel.

I will not attack GRE this fall. F GRE will hold, and A BUL will support A CON holding against any attack. A CON is already in CON, and I need to secure that center; please keep A ARM away from CON and F ION out of GRE.

Russia to England: Fall 1934 I am focused on the south and my own centers, so I cannot promise a joint Balkan move yet. I will hold RUM and WAR this fall. Let us keep talking about Italy's fleet in the west; if you move against Italian centers in Iberia or the Channel side, I will consider pressure on Italy in the Balkans next spring.

Russia to Italy: Your repeated confirmations are noted, but you have not stated exact orders for A ROM, A BUD or A BUL as requested. I will keep F BLA and A RUM defensive only while no Italian unit enters RUM, WAR, STP, UKR or SEV. Any such move will be answered at once. Send exact orders in writing.

Russia to Turkey: I cannot contest Italian centers this fall without exposing my own home. A RUM and F BLA remain defensive. Hold GRE with F ION and keep A ARM in place. Send me your exact orders in writing so I can judge your intentions.

Italy is poised to take GRE and reach 18. Please make any possible attack on an Italian-held center this fall; even a move against a weak western position could stop the win. I will contest GRE with F ION and keep A ARM in place.

I will not stand down: F ION will contest GRE, and A ARM will remain in ARM. You may secure neither of my centers without resistance. If you truly intend not to pursue my remaining unit, leave GRE alone this fall and seek your final center elsewhere.
